irwin: Oh! You came to talk to ME. Okay. Okay okay okay. Here is what I know.
I have been waiting all evening for someone to ask.
I will tell you everything. I am incapable of anything else.
First — and this is important — you are doing a wonderful job.
I saw something. I have been carrying it around like a stick.
boo: Closer. I won't say it loudly.
granolia: Oh darling, sit, sit — you will not BELIEVE.
I've been dying to tell someone, and you have kind eyes.
Now I only know what I saw, but what I saw was PLENTY.
Between us — and I mean that, between us and whoever else asks —
zimothy: I'll be brief. Brevity is free.
I keep records. The records keep everyone else honest.
You want information. Information has value. Luckily for you, I'm feeling charitable.
Per my ledger — and my ledger does not lie —
I noticed it the way I notice everything: itemized.
salem: Finally. Someone with the sense to consult the only competent investigator here.
I have solved it. Sit down.
What I am about to tell you, I have verified personally, using methods.
The others will give you facts. I give you TRUTH.
I was there. In a sense. In the truest sense.

irwin: That is everything. I feel much lighter.
I hope that helps. I hope everything helps.
If you learn more, come tell me. I will act surprised.
You may pet me now. For your trouble.
I would never lie to you. I don't know how it's done.
boo: Don't quote me. Or do. It was true.
granolia: But you didn't hear it from me, dear. Officially.
Isn't it AWFUL? I've told everyone.
Of course my memory isn't what it was. It was never what it was.
Now off you go — and send someone else over, I'm on a roll.
I'd swear to it. On somebody's grave. There's a fresh one, I hear.
zimothy: Verify it if you like. Verification is billed separately.
The rest is in the ledger, and the ledger is not for browsing.
You'll find I'm rarely wrong. It would be too expensive.
salem: You may thank me for solving this.
Nobody listens to the cat. History will.
Cross-reference it if you must. It will hold. It always holds.
I'd stake my ninth life on it. The others are spoken for.
Tell no one. Tell everyone. It changes nothing — I am right.

opener.what: The FIRST sentence of a cat's testimony — spoken before any information. Pure personality, zero facts.
opener.test: Would it make sense in front of ANY secret?
examples: Shut the door. This stays between us and the fireplace.
I wasn't going to say anything. That lasted an hour.

closer.what: The LAST sentence — the sign-off after the information lands. Deflection, running gag, mic drop.
closer.test: Would it make sense after ANY secret?
examples: And that is the last I'll speak of it. Until asked again.
Now if you'll excuse me, the sunbeam is moving.

echo_frame.what: A news-broadcast wrapper. You write the announcer's sentence; the sealed fragment fills the ███.
echo_frame.test: Read it in a radio voice — the ███ sits where the juicy part goes.
examples: ...neighbors speak of ███, though never above a whisper...
...the constable was asked about ███ and chose to examine his boots...

room.what: Rooms of the manor — dropped in as WHERE it happened.
room.test: Any Victorian-sounding room pairs with any incident.

time.what: Times of day — dropped in as WHEN it happened.
time.test: Proper o'clock or dramatic vagueness, both useful.

duration.test: Absurdly short and absurdly long are both funny.
examples: the better part of a sermon

place.what: Spots OUT IN TOWN — shops, venues, institutions.
place.test: Anywhere a Victorian could have a bad day in public.

crowd.test: From one soul to all of society — range helps the shuffle.
examples: two maids and a startled gardener
